newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-SECOND GOLD FOR ROLPH IN EUROPEAN RECORD TIME.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-SECOND GOLD FOR ROLPH IN EUROPEAN RECORD TIME.

text.p: Britain's Susan Rolph equalled a European record to claim her second gold medal on the final day of the European sprints and short-course swimming championships on Sunday.

Rolph, who won Saturday's 100 metres individual medley, took the 200 individual medley in two minutes 10.60 seconds to match the mark set by East German Petra Schneider in Gainesville, Florida, on January 8, 1982.
Fellow Briton Mark Foster also sped away with his second gold medal of the four-day championships with a storming win in the men's 50 metres freestyle.
Foster, winner of Saturday's 50 metres butterfly, qualified third in the morning's heats but proved fastest when it really mattered.
The 26-year-old Briton, 50 freestyle world short-course champion in 1993, got away to a good start and showed clearly ahead when he came out of the turn in the 25-metre Neptun pool.
Foster clocked 22.25 to win from Rene Gusperti of Italy ( 22.51) and Dmitry Kalinovsky of Belarus (22.57).
Spain's Barbara Franco brought Johanna Sjoberg's winning streak to an end by beating the 18-year-old Swede in the women's 200 metres butterfly.
Sjoberg set European records in winning the 50 and 100 butterfly on Friday and Saturday but just failed to complete the treble.
Sjoberg led clearly for the first six lengths of the eight-length race.

But Florida-based Franco, the fastest qualifier in the morning's heats, hit back in the final 50 metres, caught the Swede with one length to go and pulled away to win Spain's first-ever women's senior international championship title.
Franco clocked two minutes 10.20 seconds, with Sjoberg second in 2:10.92 and Maria Palaez completing a great race for Spain by taking the bronze in 2:11.36.
Vera Lischka claimed Austria's first international swimming title by winning the women's 50 breaststroke in 31.36 ahead of Terrie Miller of Norway, reversing the order of Friday's 100 breaststroke.
Alexander Goukov gave Belarus their first win in the men's 200 metres breaststroke, coming through strongly to take the gold in 2:09.86.
Thomas Rupprath claimed Germany's 11th title of the four-day championships, leading Fabian Hieronimus home in a German one-two in the men's 100 butterfly.
Marcel Wouda of the Netherlands completed a Rostock individual medley treble by winning the 400 event in 4:08.90.
